title: How Justin Welsh built a LinkedIn, Twitter and email audience: the creator funnel and one-platform-first approach
summary: Justin explains how he grew on LinkedIn by writing daily, then used that audience to bootstrap Twitter and a newsletter. He lays out his creator funnel (awareness, trust, deepening relationship, monetization), why a narrow niche and real craft matter, and how he pre-sells cheap, fast products based on audience demand.

principles.text: Pick one platform you enjoy and master it before adding others; skills transfer and make the next platform faster.
principles.quote: pick one platform that you like to be on so the biggest thing i see is like i heard tik tok is popular should i be on it well do you like doing videos no then no like do what you like to do

principles.text: Run a creator funnel: awareness, then trust (newsletter), then deepening relationships (community), then monetization.
principles.quote: i think of that awareness and discovery at the top trust building in the middle and then relationship deepening in the end and i think if you do those things really effectively you're able to build a really great business

principles.text: Stay in the awareness and trust phase longer before selling; a large audience of the right people gives enormous leverage.
principles.quote: stick to growing that awareness and that trust before you monetize or build a community or anything like that

principles.text: Get narrow: say one thing a thousand ways so readers instantly self-select in or out of your content.
principles.quote: learn how to say one thing a thousand ways it's better than saying a thousand things one way

principles.text: Use your existing audience to seed a new platform, then siphon followers into an email list you own.
principles.quote: i would pull 50 000 people out of their inbox and into a tweet thread and that was able for me to sort of get that tweet thread moving

principles.text: Pre-sell products and only build once enough people have paid; build what customers ask for, not what you want.
principles.quote: i never build anything unless i make a certain amount of money on it and i'll go out and say this is coming in 45 days like it's on sale right now grab it and as soon as i cross a threshold i'll go out and build it
